records.source: וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיְדַבֵּ֛ר אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה אֶל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And went Moses and spoke the words the these to all Israel.
pieces: Then Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.

L.1: And Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.

R.1: Moses went and spoke these words to all the people of Israel.

decisions.choice: Moses went and spoke (the traditional Hebrew text)
alternatives: Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel (a Dead Sea Scroll and the Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text reads "Moses went and spoke these words". One of the Dead Sea Scrolls of Deuteronomy and the ancient Greek translation read instead "Moses finished speaking all these words to all Israel". In Hebrew the two readings differ only in the order of a few letters. The other reading would make this verse close the speech of chapters 29-30, in the way 31:24 and 32:45 mark an ending. We follow the traditional Hebrew text, which makes the verse introduce the words that follow. This account of the evidence is from general knowledge and must be checked against the textual sources before review.

decisions.choice: went and spoke: set about speaking; these words point ahead to verses 2-6
decisions.reason: The verb "went" often begins a new action without a journey: Moses turns to a new task. In the traditional text "these words" are the words that follow, Moses' farewell charge to the people in verses 2-6.

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "All Israel" means the whole people. Readable says so in plain words.

records.heading: Joshua to go before the people

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם בֶּן־מֵאָה֩ וְעֶשְׂרִ֨ים שָׁנָ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ הַיּ֔וֹם לֹא־אוּכַ֥ל ע֖וֹד לָצֵ֣את וְלָב֑וֹא וַֽיהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י לֹ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֥ן הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, son of a hundred and twenty years [am] I today; not I am able any longer to go out and to come in; and Yahweh has said to me, not you will cross the Jordan the this.
pieces: He said to them, "I am 120 years old today. I can no longer go out and come in before you, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told me, 'You will not cross this Jordan.'

L.2: And he said to them, "I [am] a son of 120 years today. I am no longer able to go out and to come in, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said to me, 'You shall not cross this Jordan.'

R.2: He said to them, "I am 120 years old now. I can no longer lead you. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has told me, 'You will not cross the Jordan River.'

decisions.choice: go out and come in: lead the people in war and in their daily life
decisions.reason: The pair of verbs describes a leader's whole work, going out at the head of the people and bringing them back (Numbers 27:17; Joshua 14:11). Moses is not saying that his body has failed, since 34:7 says his strength had not left him. He is saying that his time to lead is over, because God has said he will not cross.

decisions.choice: You shall not cross this Jordan: God's earlier word to Moses
decisions.reason: God refused to let Moses enter the land because of what happened at Meribah (Numbers 20:12), and refused again when Moses pleaded with him (3:23-27; 1:37).

decisions.choice: a son of 120 years: 120 years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being the "son" of so many years.

decisions.choice: go out and come in before you; Readable "lead you"
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the Hebrew pair and adds "before you" to show it is about leading the people. Readable says what the pair means.

records.source: יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ ה֣וּא׀עֹבֵ֣ר לְפָנֶ֗יךָ הֽוּא־יַשְׁמִ֞יד אֶת־הַגּוֹיִ֥ם הָאֵ֛לֶּה מִלְּפָנֶ֖יךָ וִֽירִשְׁתָּ֑ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ ה֚וּא עֹבֵ֣ר לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Yahweh your God, he [is] crossing before you; he will destroy the nations the these from before you, and you will dispossess them; Joshua, he [is] crossing before you, just as spoke Yahweh.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} is the one who will cross over before you. He will wipe out these nations in your path, and you will drive them out. Joshua too will cross over at your head, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has said.

L.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the one crossing over before you; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will destroy these nations from before you, and you shall dispossess them. Joshua, he [is] the one crossing over before you, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.

R.3: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will go across ahead of you. He will destroy these nations as you advance, and you will drive them out. Joshua will also go ahead of you, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised.

decisions.choice: he ... he: God himself goes first, and Joshua goes with the people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets an emphatic "he" before God's crossing and another before Joshua's. God is the one who really goes ahead and wins the battles; Joshua leads the people under him. Moses' absence will not leave Israel without a leader.

decisions.choice: dispossess them: drive the nations out and take over what they held
decisions.reason: With nations as its object this verb means to drive them out and take their place (as in 9:1; 11:23). It is the same verb used for Israel taking possession of the land.

decisions.choice: as the LORD has spoken: God's appointment of Joshua
decisions.reason: God told Moses to appoint Joshua as his successor (Numbers 27:18-23) and to encourage him because he would lead the people across (1:38; 3:28).

decisions.choice: himself; "Joshua too" / "Joshua will also"
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the stress of the Hebrew "he" with "himself". "Too" and "also" show that Joshua goes ahead as well, under God.

records.source: וְעָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לָהֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֗ה לְסִיח֥וֹן וּלְע֛וֹג מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֱמֹרִ֖י וּלְאַרְצָ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁמִ֖יד אֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And will do Yahweh to them just as he did to Sihon and to Og, kings of the Amorites, and to their land, whom he destroyed them.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will deal with them as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dealt with Sihon and Og, the Amorite kings, and with their land, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroyed them.

L.4: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do to them just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroyed them.

R.4: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will destroy them, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} destroyed Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and their land.

decisions.choice: Sihon and Og: the two kings defeated east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel defeated Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan and took their land (2:26-3:11; Numbers 21:21-35). Those victories are proof of what God will do west of the river (3:21).

decisions.choice: whom he destroyed: the kings, with their land
decisions.reason: The closing clause looks back to the kings and their land together: God destroyed them and their rule.

records.source: וּנְתָנָ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה לִפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם לָהֶ֔ם כְּכָל־הַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי אֶתְכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And will give them Yahweh before you, and you will do to them according to all the commandment which I have commanded you.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will hand them over to you, and you must deal with them exactly as I have commanded you.

L.5: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will give them over before you, and you shall do to them according to all the commandment that I have commanded you.

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will let you defeat them. Then you must do to them everything I have commanded you.

decisions.choice: give them before you: put them in your power
decisions.reason: To "give" an enemy "before" someone is to let that person defeat them (2:33; 7:2, 23).

decisions.choice: all the commandment I have commanded you: the orders about the nations of the land
decisions.reason: "Commandment" is singular, the whole charge Moses has given. Here it points to the orders for dealing with the nations of the land: to make no covenant with them, to destroy their altars and to devote them to destruction (7:1-5; 20:16-18).

decisions.choice: exactly as / everything I have commanded
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "according to all the commandment". Balanced and Readable fold the singular noun into the verb, which says the same thing.

records.source: חִזְק֣וּ וְאִמְצ֔וּ אַל־תִּֽירְא֥וּ וְאַל־תַּעַרְצ֖וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֑ם כִּ֣י׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ ה֚וּא הַהֹלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֥א יַרְפְּךָ֖ וְלֹ֥א יַעַזְבֶֽךָּ׃פ
records.gloss: Be strong and be bold; do not fear and do not tremble from before them, for Yahweh your God, he [is] the [one] going with you; not he will let you drop, and not he will forsake you.
pieces: Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid of them or tremble before them, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is the one who goes with you. He will not let you go, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not abandon you."

L.6: Be strong and be courageous; do not fear and do not tremble before them, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the one who goes with you. He will not let you go, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not forsake you."

R.6: Be strong and brave! Do not be afraid of them or let them frighten you. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God is going with you. He will not let go of you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not leave you on your own."

decisions.choice: be strong and be bold: stand firm and have courage
decisions.reason: The two verbs together are the charge to hold firm and act bravely in the face of danger. Moses gives it here to the whole people, and then to Joshua (verses 7, 23; 3:28; Joshua 1:6-9).

decisions.choice: let you drop: let go of you, loosen his hold
decisions.reason: The first verb means to let something fall slack, to let go of it. The second means to leave behind or abandon. Together they promise that God will not loosen his grip on his people or leave them on their own (verse 8; Joshua 1:5).

decisions.choice: you: the people, plural and then singular
decisions.reason: The commands are plural, spoken to all the people. "Your God" and "with you" are singular, as Deuteronomy often speaks to Israel as one person.

decisions.choice: let you go / let go of you
decisions.reason: The English keeps the picture of loosening a hold, which the Hebrew verb has, instead of a more general word such as "fail".

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה לִֽיהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו לְעֵינֵ֣י כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֘לחֲזַ֣ק וֶאֱמָץ֒ כִּ֣י אַתָּ֗ה תָּבוֹא֙ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה לַאֲבֹתָ֖ם לָתֵ֣ת לָהֶ֑ם וְאַתָּ֖ה תַּנְחִילֶ֥נָּה אוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And called Moses to Joshua and said to him in [the] eyes of all Israel, be strong and be bold, for you will go with the people the this into the land which swore Yahweh to their fathers to give to them, and you will cause them to inherit it.
pieces: Then Moses summoned Joshua and, with all Israel looking on, said to him, "Be strong and courageous. You are the one who will go with this people into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to their ancestors to give them, and you will divide it among them as their inheritance.

L.7: And Moses called Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and be courageous, for you shall go with this people into the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to their fathers to give to them, and you shall cause them to inherit it.

R.7: Then Moses called for Joshua. With all Israel watching, he said to him, "Be strong and brave. You will go with these people into the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised with an oath to give their ancestors. You will give it to them as their own.

decisions.choice: in the sight of all Israel: a public commissioning
decisions.reason: Moses hands over the leadership before the whole people, so that everyone knows who will lead them and that he has Moses' authority (Numbers 27:19-20).

decisions.choice: cause them to inherit it: lead them in and share out the land
decisions.reason: As in 1:38 and 3:28, the verb means to give others an inheritance. Joshua will bring the people into the land and divide it among the tribes (Joshua 14:1).

decisions.choice: you will go with this people (the traditional Hebrew text)
alternatives: you will bring this people (Samaritan Pentateuch, some ancient translations)
decisions.reason: The traditional Hebrew text reads "you will go with this people". The Samaritan Pentateuch and some ancient translations read "you will bring this people", with the same verb God uses in verse 23. The difference is one small change of vowels and a letter. We follow the traditional text. This account of the evidence is from general knowledge and must be checked against the textual sources before review.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "fathers", meaning forefathers. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", as in 1:8.

records.source: וַֽיהוָ֞ה ה֣וּא׀הַהֹלֵ֣ךְ לְפָנֶ֗יךָ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔ךְ לֹ֥א יַרְפְּךָ֖ וְלֹ֣א יַֽעַזְבֶ֑ךָּ לֹ֥א תִירָ֖א וְלֹ֥א תֵחָֽת׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh, he [is] the [one] going before you; he will be with you; not he will let you drop, and not he will forsake you; not you shall fear, and not you shall be dismayed.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} goes ahead of you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be with you. He will not let you go or abandon you. Do not be afraid or lose heart."

L.8: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] the one who goes before you; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be with you. He will not let you go, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not forsake you. Do not fear, and do not be dismayed."

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will lead the way for you. He will be with you. He will not let go of you or leave you on your own. So do not be afraid, and do not lose heart."

decisions.choice: you: now Joshua alone
decisions.reason: Every "you" in this verse is singular and speaks to Joshua. He receives in person the promise Moses has just given to all the people in verse 6, almost word for word.

decisions.choice: be dismayed: be shattered, lose heart
decisions.reason: The verb means to be broken or shattered, and of people to be terrified or lose all courage (1:21; Joshua 1:9).

decisions.choice: himself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the stress of the Hebrew "he" with "himself", as in verse 3.

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Readable adds "So" to show that the commands follow from the promise.

records.source: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב מֹשֶׁה֮ אֶת־הַתּוֹרָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֒ וַֽיִּתְּנָ֗הּ אֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ בְּנֵ֣י לֵוִ֔י הַנֹּ֣שְׂאִ֔ים אֶת־אֲר֖וֹן בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶל־כָּל־זִקְנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And wrote Moses the law the this and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, the [ones] carrying the ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh, and to all [the] elders of Israel.
pieces: Then Moses put this law in writing. He handed it to the priests, the descendants of Levi, who were the bearers of the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and to all of Israel's elders.

L.9: And Moses wrote this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and to all the elders of Israel.

R.9: Moses wrote down this teaching. He gave it to the priests from the tribe of Levi, the men who carried the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He also gave it to all the leaders of Israel.

decisions.choice: this law: the whole of Moses' teaching in this book
decisions.reason: As in 1:5, "law" is instruction: the whole body of Moses' teaching, history and appeal as well as rules. Now it is set down in writing (verse 24; 17:18).

decisions.choice: the priests who carried the ark
decisions.reason: The tribe of Levi was set apart to carry the ark (10:8), and in the crossing of the Jordan the priests carry it (Joshua 3:3). Giving the written law to the priests and the elders puts it in the care of both the religious and the civil leaders.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "teaching" for the Hebrew word Literal and Balanced render "law", as in 1:5.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable calls the elders "leaders", which says what they were: the senior men who led the tribes and towns.

records.source: וַיְצַ֥ו מֹשֶׁ֖ה אוֹתָ֣ם לֵאמֹ֑ר מִקֵּ֣ץ׀שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֗ים בְּמֹעֵ֛ד שְׁנַ֥ת הַשְּׁמִטָּ֖ה בְּחַ֥ג הַסֻּכּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And commanded Moses them, saying, at [the] end of seven years, at [the] appointed time of [the] year of the release, at [the] festival of the booths,
pieces: Moses gave them this command: "At the end of every seven years, at the set time of the year of release, during the Festival of Booths,

L.10: And Moses commanded them, saying, "At the end of seven years, at the appointed time of the year of release, at the festival of booths,

R.10: Moses gave them this order: "Every seven years, in the year when debts are canceled, at the Festival of Booths,

decisions.choice: at the end of seven years: in the seventh year
decisions.reason: As in 15:1, "at the end of seven years" means in the last year of each seven, the year of release, not after it.

decisions.choice: the year of release: the seventh year, when debts were canceled
decisions.reason: Every seventh year Israelites were to release their fellow Israelites from debts (15:1-3). The same word is used of letting the land rest in the seventh year (Exodus 23:11).

decisions.choice: the festival of booths: the autumn harvest festival
decisions.reason: The festival was held for seven days after the harvest, at the place God would choose; the people lived in shelters made of branches to remember the wilderness journey (16:13-15; Leviticus 23:33-43). In the year of release the whole nation would be gathered there.

decisions.choice: the year when debts are canceled
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the year of release was.

records.source: בְּב֣וֹא כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֵרָאוֹת֙ אֶת־פְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בַּמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִבְחָ֑ר תִּקְרָ֞א אֶת־הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּ֛את נֶ֥גֶד כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּאָזְנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: when comes all Israel to appear [before] the face of Yahweh your God in the place which he will choose, you will read the law the this before all Israel in their ears.
pieces: when all Israel comes to appear before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at the place of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} choosing, you must read this law aloud to all Israel, so that they hear it.

L.11: when all Israel comes to appear before the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at the place that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will choose, you shall read this law before all Israel in their hearing.

R.11: when all Israel comes to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God at the place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses, you must read this teaching aloud to all of them.

decisions.choice: the place he will choose: the one place of worship
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy looks ahead to one place where God will put his name and where Israel will bring its offerings and keep its festivals (12:5; 16:16).

decisions.choice: to appear before the LORD
decisions.reason: The vowels of the traditional text read the verb as "to be seen", that is, to appear before the LORD, as in 16:16. The same consonants could be read "to see the face of the LORD". The sense is the same: the people come before God at his sanctuary.

decisions.choice: you shall read: singular
decisions.reason: "You" is singular. It may speak to Israel as one, or to the leader who will stand before the people. The reading was done by a leader in later times (Joshua 8:34-35; 2 Kings 23:2; Nehemiah 8:1-3).

decisions.choice: aloud ... so that they hear it
decisions.reason: "In their ears" means in their hearing. Balanced and Readable say the reading was aloud, for all to hear.

decisions.choice: stand before
decisions.reason: Readable says "stand before" for the less common "appear before".

records.source: הַקְהֵ֣ל אֶת־הָעָ֗ם הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֤ים וְהַנָּשִׁים֙ וְהַטַּ֔ף וְגֵרְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֑יךָ לְמַ֨עַן יִשְׁמְע֜וּ וּלְמַ֣עַן יִלְמְד֗וּ וְיָֽרְאוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וְשָֽׁמְר֣וּ לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵ֖י הַתּוֹרָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
records.gloss: Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones and your sojourner who [is] in your gates, so that they may hear and so that they may learn, and they will fear Yahweh your God and take care to do all [the] words of the law the this.
pieces: Gather the people together, men, women and children, and the outsiders who live in your towns, so that they may hear and learn, and fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and carefully obey all the words of this law.

L.12: Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and your sojourner who [is] within your gates, so that they may hear and so that they may learn, and fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and take care to do all the words of this law.

R.12: Bring all the people together: men, women, children, and the outsiders living in your towns. Then they will hear and learn to fear and honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. They will be careful to obey everything this teaching says.

decisions.choice: the little ones: the children
decisions.reason: The word means small children, those too young to march or fight. The whole community is gathered, not only the men.

decisions.choice: sojourner: a foreigner living among Israel
decisions.reason: The word names someone from another people who has settled among Israel without land of his own, and whom the law protects (10:18-19; 14:29). Such people also hear the law.

decisions.choice: fear the LORD and take care to do: reverence that shows in obedience
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to hold him in awe and respect, and Deuteronomy ties it to keeping his words (4:10; 6:2, 24). Hearing leads to learning, learning to fear, and fear to obedience.

decisions.choice: the outsiders who live in your towns
decisions.reason: "Sojourner" is uncommon in modern English. "Your gates" means your towns, whose gates were where public life went on.

decisions.choice: fear and honor
decisions.reason: Readable adds "honor" so that "fear" is not taken as mere terror, as in 17:19.

records.source: וּבְנֵיהֶ֞ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יָדְע֗וּ יִשְׁמְעוּ֙ וְלָ֣מְד֔וּ לְיִרְאָ֖ה אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם כָּל־הַיָּמִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֤ם חַיִּים֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֜ם עֹבְרִ֧ים אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֛ן שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃פ
records.gloss: And their children who not have known will hear and learn to fear Yahweh your God all the days which you [are] alive on the land which you [are] crossing the Jordan there to possess it.
pieces: Their children, who do not yet know it, will hear it too and learn to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of."

L.13: And their children, who have not known [it], will hear and learn to fear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God all the days that you live on the land that you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of [it]."

R.13: Their children, who have never heard it, will hear it too. They will learn to fear and honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God for as long as you live in the land across the Jordan River that you are going to take as your own."

decisions.choice: who have not known: who do not yet know the law
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. The children have not yet come to know God's law, nor seen for themselves what God did for Israel (11:2). The public reading is how each new generation learns it.

decisions.choice: all the days you live: for as long as Israel lives in the land
decisions.reason: "You" is plural and means Israel through its generations. The reading is to go on as long as the people live in the land.

decisions.choice: it
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "know". Literal brackets it.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֗ה הֵ֣ן קָרְב֣וּ יָמֶיךָ֮ לָמוּת֒ קְרָ֣א אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֛וּ בְּאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד וַאֲצַוֶּ֑נּוּ וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ מֹשֶׁה֙ וִֽיהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וַיִּֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ בְּאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, look, have drawn near your days to die; call Joshua and present yourselves at [the] tent of meeting, that I may commission him. And went Moses and Joshua and presented themselves at [the] tent of meeting.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "The time of your death is near. Call Joshua, and the two of you come and stand at the tent of meeting, so that I can commission him." So Moses and Joshua went and took their places at the tent of meeting.

L.14: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Look, your days to die have drawn near. Call Joshua, and present yourselves at the tent of meeting, that I may charge him." And Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the tent of meeting.

R.14: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "You will soon die. Call Joshua, and come together to the meeting tent. There I will give him his orders." So Moses and Joshua went and stood at the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: commission him: charge him with his task and give him authority
decisions.reason: The verb means to command, and with a person as its object to appoint him to a work and give him his orders (3:28; Numbers 27:19, 23). God now does in person what Moses has done in verse 7. The commissioning itself is told in verse 23.

decisions.choice: present yourselves: take your stand before God
decisions.reason: The verb means to station oneself, to stand ready, used of standing before God to meet him (Exodus 19:17; 1 Samuel 10:19).

decisions.choice: the tent of meeting: where God met Moses
decisions.reason: The tent was where God met with Moses and spoke with him (Exodus 33:7-11). This is the only time Deuteronomy mentions it.

decisions.choice: the meeting tent
decisions.reason: Readable says "the meeting tent", as in Exodus and Numbers.

records.heading: Joshua commissioned at the tent of meeting

records.source: וַיֵּרָ֧א יְהוָ֛ה בָּאֹ֖הֶל בְּעַמּ֣וּד עָנָ֑ן וַיַּעֲמֹ֛ד עַמּ֥וּד הֶעָנָ֖ן עַל־פֶּ֥תַח הָאֹֽהֶל׃ס
records.gloss: And appeared Yahweh at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and stood [the] pillar of the cloud over [the] entrance of the tent.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared in a pillar of cloud at the tent, and the pillar stood over its entrance.

L.15: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the entrance of the tent.

R.15: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} appeared there in a tall column of cloud. The cloud stood at the entrance of the tent.

decisions.choice: a pillar of cloud: the sign of God's presence
decisions.reason: The pillar of cloud led Israel out of Egypt and through the wilderness (Exodus 13:21-22), and it came down at the entrance of the tent when God spoke with Moses (Exodus 33:9-10; Numbers 12:5).

decisions.choice: over the entrance: above it, or at it
decisions.reason: The word can mean "over" or "by, at". Either way the cloud stands at the doorway of the tent, as in Exodus 33:9.

decisions.choice: a tall column of cloud
decisions.reason: Readable says "column" for "pillar", a plainer word for the same shape.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה הִנְּךָ֥ שֹׁכֵ֖ב עִם־אֲבֹתֶ֑יךָ וְקָם֩ הָעָ֨ם הַזֶּ֜ה וְזָנָ֣ה׀אַחֲרֵ֣י׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י נֵֽכַר־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר ה֤וּא בָא־שָׁ֨מָּה֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ וַעֲזָבַ֕נִי וְהֵפֵר֙ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖תִּי אִתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, look, you [are] lying down with your fathers, and will rise the people the this and will prostitute after [the] gods of [the] foreignness of the land which it [is] going there into its midst, and it will forsake me and break my covenant which I made with it.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "You are about to rest with your ancestors. Then this people will rise up and prostitute themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will abandon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and break {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, which I made with them.

L.16: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Look, you are about to lie down with your fathers, and this people will rise up and prostitute themselves after the foreign gods of the land into whose midst they are going, and they will forsake {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and break {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant that I made with them.

R.16: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "You will soon die. After that, these people will be unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, like a wife who leaves her husband for other men. They will chase after the gods of the foreign land they are going into. They will abandon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and break the covenant I made with them.

decisions.choice: lie down with your fathers: die
decisions.reason: To "lie down with" one's fathers is a common way of speaking of death (Genesis 47:30; 1 Kings 2:10).

decisions.choice: prostitute themselves: be unfaithful to God by worshiping other gods
decisions.reason: The verb means to act as a prostitute. The covenant is pictured as a marriage, so turning to other gods is unfaithfulness to God, who is like a husband to his people (Exodus 34:15-16; Judges 2:17; Hosea 2:4-7).

decisions.choice: it: the people as one body
decisions.reason: God speaks of "this people" with singular verbs and pronouns, "it will forsake me", as of one person. The sense is the whole people together.

decisions.choice: break my covenant: undo the covenant from Israel's side
decisions.reason: The verb means to break or make void. The covenant God made at Horeb and renewed in Moab (5:2; 28:69) binds Israel to worship God alone; turning to other gods breaks it (Leviticus 26:15).

decisions.choice: like a wife who leaves her husband for other men
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture behind "prostitute themselves" rather than using the word, which young readers may not understand in this sense.

decisions.choice: rest with your ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the gentle picture of death as lying down, with "rest". Literal keeps "lie down with your fathers".

records.heading: Write down this song

records.source: וְחָרָ֣ה אַפִּ֣י ב֣וֹ בַיּוֹם־הַ֠הוּא וַעֲזַבְתִּ֞ים וְהִסְתַּרְתִּ֨י פָנַ֤י מֵהֶם֙ וְהָיָ֣ה לֶֽאֱכֹ֔ל וּמְצָאֻ֛הוּ רָע֥וֹת רַבּ֖וֹת וְצָר֑וֹת וְאָמַר֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא הֲלֹ֗א עַ֣ל כִּֽי־אֵ֤ין אֱלֹהַי֙ בְּקִרְבִּ֔י מְצָא֖וּנִי הָרָע֥וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And will burn my anger against it on the day the that, and I will forsake them and hide my face from them, and it will be for devouring, and will find it evils many and troubles; and it will say on the day the that, [is it] not because not my God [is] in my midst [that] have found me the evils the these?
pieces: On that day {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger will blaze against them. I will abandon them and hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them, and they will be devoured. Many disasters and troubles will overtake them, and on that day they will say, 'Have these disasters not come on us because our God is no longer with us?'

L.17: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger will burn against them on that day, and I will forsake them and hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them, and they will be [given over] to be devoured, and many evils and troubles will find them. And they will say on that day, 'Is it not because my God [is] not in my midst [that] these evils have found me?'

R.17: When that happens, I will be very angry with them. I will leave them and turn away from them. They will be destroyed, and many terrible troubles will come on them. Then they will say, 'These troubles have come on us because our God is not with us anymore!'

decisions.choice: hide my face: withdraw my favor and help
decisions.reason: When God's face shines on his people he blesses and protects them (Numbers 6:25-26). To hide his face is to turn away and leave them without his help (32:20; Isaiah 54:8).

decisions.choice: for devouring: to be eaten up, destroyed
decisions.reason: The people will become prey to be devoured. The verse does not say by whom; the curses of 28:25-68 and the Song (32:23-25) speak of enemies, hunger and disease.

decisions.choice: my God, my midst, found me: the people speaking as one
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, the people are one body, and in their complaint they say "my God" and "found me". The sense is "our God" and "found us".

decisions.choice: our God is not with us: true, but only half the truth
decisions.reason: The people will see that God has left them, but verse 18 gives the reason they leave out: he hides his face because they turned to other gods.

decisions.choice: us, our
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the plural, which says what the singular means when the people speak as one. Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: turn away from them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "hide my face"; Literal and Balanced keep it.

records.source: וְאָנֹכִ֗י הַסְתֵּ֨ר אַסְתִּ֤יר פָּנַי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא עַ֥ל כָּל־הָרָעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה כִּ֣י פָנָ֔ה אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲחֵרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I, hiding I will hide my face on the day the that, because of all the evil which it has done, for it has turned to gods other.
pieces: Yes, I will certainly hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face on that day because of all the evil they have done in turning to other gods.

L.18: And I will surely hide {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face on that day because of all the evil that they have done, for they have turned to other gods.

R.18: I will surely turn away from them at that time, because of all the evil they have done by worshiping other gods.

decisions.choice: I will surely hide: strong emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets "I" first and doubles the verb, "hiding I will hide". God answers the people's complaint (verse 17): yes, he has hidden his face, and he has done it on purpose.

decisions.choice: for it has turned: what the evil is
decisions.reason: The last clause names the evil they have done: turning to other gods.

decisions.choice: worshiping
decisions.reason: Readable says what "turning to" other gods means.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה כִּתְב֤וּ לָכֶם֙ אֶת־הַשִּׁירָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וְלַמְּדָ֥הּ אֶת־בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שִׂימָ֣הּ בְּפִיהֶ֑ם לְמַ֨עַן תִּהְיֶה־לִּ֜י הַשִּׁירָ֥ה הַזֹּ֛את לְעֵ֖ד בִּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And now write for yourselves the song the this and teach it [to] the sons of Israel; put it in their mouths, so that may be for me the song the this as a witness against [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: So now write down this song for yourselves, and teach it to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Put it on their lips, so that this song will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witness against the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.19: And now write for yourselves this song, and teach it to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel; put it in their mouths, so that this song may be for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a witness against the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.19: Now write down this song, both of you, and teach it to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Help them learn it by heart, so that this song will be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witness against them.

decisions.choice: write: plural; teach and put: singular
decisions.reason: "Write" is plural and speaks to Moses and Joshua together. "Teach" and "put" are singular and speak to Moses, who writes and teaches the song in verse 22.

decisions.choice: put it in their mouths: make them able to recite it
decisions.reason: The people are to know the song so well that they can say it from memory.

decisions.choice: a witness: one who testifies in a covenant dispute
decisions.reason: When Israel breaks the covenant, the song will speak against them as a witness in court, as heaven and earth (30:19; 31:28) and the book of the law (verse 26) will. The song itself calls heaven and earth to listen (32:1).

decisions.choice: both of you
decisions.reason: Readable shows that "write" is plural, spoken to Moses and Joshua.

decisions.choice: put it on their lips / help them learn it by heart
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture with a more natural English phrase; Readable says what it means.

records.source: כִּֽי־אֲבִיאֶ֜נּוּ אֶֽל־הָאֲדָמָ֣ה׀אֲשֶׁר־נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתִּי לַאֲבֹתָ֗יו זָבַ֤ת חָלָב֙ וּדְבַ֔שׁ וְאָכַ֥ל וְשָׂבַ֖ע וְדָשֵׁ֑ן וּפָנָ֞ה אֶל־אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֲחֵרִים֙ וַעֲבָד֔וּם וְנִ֣אֲצ֔וּנִי וְהֵפֵ֖ר אֶת־בְּרִיתִֽי׃
records.gloss: For I will bring it into the land which I swore to its fathers, flowing [with] milk and honey, and it will eat and be satisfied and grow fat, and it will turn to gods other and they will serve them, and they will spurn me and it will break my covenant.
pieces: For when I have brought them into the land flowing with milk and honey that I swore to give their ancestors, and they have eaten their fill and grown fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them. They will treat {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with contempt and break {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant.

L.20: For I will bring them into the land that I swore to their fathers, flowing [with] milk and honey, and they will eat and be satisfied and grow fat, and they will turn to other gods and serve them, and they will despise {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and break {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant.

R.20: I will bring them into the land I promised with an oath to give their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey. They will have plenty to eat and grow rich and comfortable. Then they will turn to other gods and worship them. They will reject {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and break {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant.

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: a rich and fertile land
decisions.reason: Milk from flocks and herds and honey from bees or fruit stand for a land of plenty (6:3; Exodus 3:8).

decisions.choice: eat and be satisfied and grow fat: prosperity that leads to forgetting God
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy warns that when Israel has plenty it may forget the God who gave it (6:10-12; 8:10-14). The Song says the same: "Jeshurun grew fat and kicked" (32:15).

decisions.choice: spurn: treat with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to despise or scorn, to treat as worthless (Numbers 14:11, 23).

decisions.choice: for: why the song is needed
decisions.reason: The verse gives the reason for the song in verse 19: God already knows what Israel will do in the land.

decisions.choice: grow rich and comfortable
decisions.reason: Readable explains "grow fat", a picture of wealth and ease.

records.source: וְ֠הָיָה כִּֽי־תִמְצֶ֨אןָ אֹת֜וֹ רָע֣וֹת רַבּוֹת֮ וְצָרוֹת֒ וְ֠עָנְתָה הַשִּׁירָ֨ה הַזֹּ֤את לְפָנָיו֙ לְעֵ֔ד כִּ֛י לֹ֥א תִשָּׁכַ֖ח מִפִּ֣י זַרְע֑וֹ כִּ֧י יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶת־יִצְר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר ה֤וּא עֹשֶׂה֙ הַיּ֔וֹם בְּטֶ֣רֶם אֲבִיאֶ֔נּוּ אֶל־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבָּֽעְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when find it evils many and troubles, then will testify the song the this before it as a witness, for not it will be forgotten from [the] mouth of its offspring; for I know its inclination which it [is] doing today, before I bring it into the land which I swore.
pieces: And when many disasters and troubles overtake them, this song will speak against them as a witness, because their descendants will not forget it. I know what their hearts are inclined to do even now, before I have brought them into the land I swore to give them."

L.21: And it will be, when many evils and troubles have found them, that this song will testify before them as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their offspring. For I know their inclination, which they are acting on today, before I bring them into the land that I swore [to give]."

R.21: When many terrible troubles come on them, this song will stand up as a witness against them, because their descendants will still remember it. I know what they are planning to do, even today, before I bring them into the land I promised."

decisions.choice: testify: answer, speak as a witness
decisions.reason: The verb means to answer, and in a court to give evidence. The song will speak up against the people and show that their troubles are what God warned of.

decisions.choice: inclination: the bent of their thoughts and plans
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning to form or shape, and names what a person's mind is shaping, its plans and leanings (Genesis 6:5; 8:21).

decisions.choice: which it is doing today, before I bring it: already at work
decisions.reason: The bent toward unfaithfulness is not only in the future; it is at work already, before the people have entered the land.

decisions.choice: what their hearts are inclined to do
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "hearts", since the word speaks of the inner person.

decisions.choice: [to give] / to give
decisions.reason: The Hebrew ends with "I swore". English needs what God swore, as in verse 20.

records.source: וַיִּכְתֹּ֥ב מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־הַשִּׁירָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַֽיְלַמְּדָ֖הּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And wrote Moses the song the this on the day the that and taught it [to] the sons of Israel.
pieces: So Moses wrote down this song that same day and taught it to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.22: So Moses wrote this song on that day and taught it to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.22: Moses wrote the song down that day and taught it to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: this song: the Song of Moses in 32:1-43
decisions.reason: The song God told Moses to write (verse 19) is given in the next chapter. Verse 30 introduces it.

records.gloss: And he commissioned Joshua son of Nun and said, be strong and be bold, for you will bring the sons of Israel into the land which I swore to them, and I will be with you.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commissioned Joshua son of Nun. He said, "Be strong and courageous. You are the one who will bring the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} into the land I swore to give them, and I will be with you."

L.23: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} charged Joshua son of Nun and said, "Be strong and be courageous, for you shall bring the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel into the land that I swore to them, and I will be with you."

R.23: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Joshua son of Nun his orders. He said, "Be strong and brave. You will lead the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} into the land I promised them, and I will be with you."

decisions.choice: he commissioned: the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not name the subject, and Moses was the last person named (verse 22). But the speaker says "the land that I swore" and "I will be with you", which only God can say, and in verse 14 God said he would commission Joshua at the tent. So the subject is the LORD.

decisions.choice: the land I swore ... I will be with you (the traditional Hebrew text)
alternatives: Moses commissioned Joshua: the land the LORD swore, and he will be with you (Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation makes Moses the one who commissions Joshua, and reads "the land the LORD swore to them, and he will be with you". The traditional Hebrew text has God speaking in the first person, and we follow it. This account of the evidence is from general knowledge and must be checked against the textual sources before review.

decisions.choice: be strong and courageous ... I will be with you
decisions.reason: God gives Joshua the charge Moses gave him in verse 7, with his own promise of presence. He repeats both when Joshua takes command (Joshua 1:5-9).

decisions.choice: the LORD
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject the Hebrew leaves unstated (see the meaning decision). Literal keeps "he".

records.gloss: And it was, when finished Moses to write [the] words of the law the this on a book until they were complete,
pieces: When Moses had finished writing out the words of this law in a book, to the very last word,

L.24: And it happened, when Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a book to their end,

R.24: Moses finished writing all the words of this teaching on a scroll.

decisions.choice: a book: a written document, a scroll
decisions.reason: The word names any written document. A book of this kind was written on a scroll of leather or papyrus, not bound in pages (17:18; Jeremiah 36:2).

decisions.choice: until they were complete: all of it, to the end
decisions.reason: The phrase means Moses wrote the whole of it, leaving nothing out. The same phrase closes verse 30.

decisions.choice: and it happened, when Moses had finished: leading into verse 25
decisions.reason: The verse sets the time for what follows: once the writing was done, Moses gave his order to the Levites. Verse 9 already said that Moses wrote the law; this verse takes the story up again.

decisions.choice: scroll
decisions.reason: Readable says "scroll" so that readers picture the right kind of book, as in 17:18.

records.source: וַיְצַ֤ו מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶת־הַלְוִיִּ֔ם נֹ֥שְׂאֵ֛יאֲר֥וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: then commanded Moses the Levites, carriers of [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh, saying,
pieces: he gave this order to the Levites, the bearers of the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}:

L.25: that Moses commanded the Levites, the carriers of the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying,

R.25: Then he gave an order to the Levites, whose job was to carry the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said,

decisions.choice: the Levites who carried the ark: the priests of verse 9
decisions.reason: Verse 9 calls those who carry the ark "the priests, the sons of Levi". Deuteronomy speaks of priests and Levites together as the tribe set apart for this duty (10:8; 18:1).

records.source: לָקֹ֗חַ אֵ֣ת סֵ֤פֶר הַתּוֹרָה֙ הַזֶּ֔ה וְשַׂמְתֶּ֣ם אֹת֔וֹ מִצַּ֛ד אֲר֥וֹן בְּרִית־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָֽיָה־שָׁ֥ם בְּךָ֖ לְעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: Take [the] book of the law the this and put it at [the] side of [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh your God, and it will be there against you as a witness.
pieces: "Take this book of the law and set it next to the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Let it stay there as a witness against you.

L.26: "Take this book of the law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and it shall be there as a witness against you.

R.26: "Take this scroll of teaching and put it next to the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. It will stay there as a witness against you.

decisions.choice: beside the ark: next to it, not inside
decisions.reason: The ark held only the two stone tablets of the covenant (10:1-5; 1 Kings 8:9). The book of the law is kept beside it, in the most holy place, where it cannot be lost or changed.

decisions.choice: a witness against you: the written law as evidence
decisions.reason: Like the song (verse 19), the book will stand as a witness. If Israel breaks the covenant, the written words will show what they had been told. "You" is singular: Israel as one.

decisions.choice: take: an order
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the bare form of the verb as a command, a forceful way to give an order.

decisions.choice: scroll of teaching
decisions.reason: Readable says "scroll" (verse 24) and "teaching" (1:5).

records.source: כִּ֣י אָנֹכִ֤י יָדַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֶֽת־מֶרְיְךָ֔ וְאֶֽת־עָרְפְּךָ֖ הַקָּשֶׁ֑ה הֵ֣ן בְּעוֹדֶנִּי֩ חַ֨י עִמָּכֶ֜ם הַיּ֗וֹם מַמְרִ֤ים הֱיִתֶם֙ עִם־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְאַ֖ף כִּי־אַחֲרֵ֥י מוֹתִֽי׃
records.gloss: For I, I know your rebellion and your neck the stiff; look, while I [am] still alive with you today, rebellious you have been with Yahweh, and how much more after my death!
pieces: I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. Even now, while I am still alive and with you, you have been rebelling against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. How much more will you rebel after I am dead!

L.27: For I know your rebellion and your stiff neck. Look, while I am still alive with you today, you have been rebellious against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; how much more, then, after my death!

R.27: I know how you rebel and how stubborn you are. Even today, while I am still alive and here with you, you rebel against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You will rebel even more after I die!

decisions.choice: stiff neck: stubbornness
decisions.reason: A stiff neck is the picture of an ox that will not bend to the yoke; it means stubborn refusal to obey (9:6, 13; Exodus 32:9).

decisions.choice: how much more: an argument from lesser to greater
decisions.reason: If the people rebel while Moses is still with them, they will rebel all the more when he is gone.

decisions.choice: you have been rebellious: Israel's record in the wilderness
decisions.reason: Moses has already said these words of Israel's whole journey (9:7, 24).

decisions.choice: stubborn
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "stiff neck" means. Literal keeps the picture.

records.source: הַקְהִ֧ילוּ אֵלַ֛י אֶת־כָּל־זִקְנֵ֥י שִׁבְטֵיכֶ֖ם וְשֹׁטְרֵיכֶ֑ם וַאֲדַבְּרָ֣ה בְאָזְנֵיהֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְאָעִ֣ידָה בָּ֔ם אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Assemble to me all [the] elders of your tribes and your officials, that I may speak in their ears the words the these, and I may call to witness against them the heavens and the earth.
pieces: Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, so that I can speak these words for them to hear and call heaven and earth as witnesses against them.

L.28: Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, that I may speak these words in their hearing and call the heavens and the earth to witness against them.

R.28: Bring all the leaders of your tribes and your officials here to me. I want to tell them these things, and I will call on heaven and earth to be witnesses against them.

decisions.choice: officials: officers who carried out orders
decisions.reason: These were officers who served under the leaders and judges, keeping records and passing on orders (1:15; 16:18; 20:5).

decisions.choice: heaven and earth as witnesses
decisions.reason: In a covenant, witnesses were called to confirm it. Moses calls on heaven and earth, which last for all time (4:26; 30:19). The Song opens by calling them to listen (32:1).

decisions.choice: these words: the Song that follows
decisions.reason: The words Moses will speak to the assembly are the Song (verse 30; 32:1-43).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable calls the elders "leaders", as in verse 9.

records.source: כִּ֣י יָדַ֗עְתִּי אַחֲרֵ֤י מוֹתִי֙ כִּֽי־הַשְׁחֵ֣ת תַּשְׁחִת֔וּן וְסַרְתֶּ֣ם מִן־הַדֶּ֔רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי אֶתְכֶ֑ם וְקָרָ֨את אֶתְכֶ֤ם הָֽרָעָה֙ בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַיָּמִ֔ים כִּֽי־תַעֲשׂ֤וּ אֶת־הָרַע֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לְהַכְעִיס֖וֹ בְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: For I know after my death that acting corruptly you will act corruptly and turn from the way which I have commanded you, and will meet you the evil in [the] latter [part] of the days, because you will do the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh to provoke him by [the] work of your hands.
pieces: For I know that once I am dead you will become utterly corrupt and turn aside from the way I have commanded you. In days to come disaster will strike you, because you will do what is evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and provoke {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger by what your hands have made."

L.29: For I know that after my death you will surely act corruptly and turn aside from the way that I have commanded you, and evil will meet you in the latter days, because you will do what is evil in the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, provoking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger with the work of your hands."

R.29: I know that after I die, you will become completely evil. You will turn away from the way of life I commanded you to follow. In the future, terrible trouble will come on you, because you will do what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says is evil. You will make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry by worshiping idols you have made with your own hands."

decisions.choice: you will surely act corruptly: strong emphasis
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. To act corruptly is to ruin oneself by turning to idols (4:16, 25).

decisions.choice: the latter days: the days to come
decisions.reason: The phrase means the future, the time after this (4:30). It does not here mean the end of the world.

decisions.choice: the work of your hands: idols
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy "the work of human hands" often means idols of wood and stone (4:28; 27:15), and making idols is what provokes God to anger (4:25; 9:18). The phrase can also mean a person's deeds in general.

decisions.choice: by worshiping idols you have made with your own hands
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the work of your hands" points to (see the meaning decision). Literal and Balanced keep the wider phrase.

records.gloss: And spoke Moses in [the] ears of all [the] assembly of Israel the words of the song the this until they were complete.
pieces: Then Moses recited the words of this song from beginning to end, while the whole assembly of Israel listened:

L.30: And Moses spoke in the hearing of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song to their end:

R.30: Then Moses spoke the words of this song to the whole assembly of Israel. He said all of it, from beginning to end:

decisions.choice: the words of this song: introduces 32:1-43
decisions.reason: The verse introduces the Song, which follows in the next chapter. It is the song God told Moses to write and teach (verses 19, 22).

decisions.choice: the assembly of Israel: the people gathered before Moses
decisions.reason: The word names Israel gathered together. The elders and officials of verse 28 stand for the whole people.

decisions.choice: from beginning to end
decisions.reason: "Until they were complete" means the whole song; Balanced and Readable say so in a common phrase. The rendering ends with a colon because the Song itself follows.
